subject: science
intro: When two objects at different temperatures touch or mix, thermal energy (heat) flows from the hotter object to the cooler one. This continues until both objects reach the same temperature, a state called thermal equilibrium. The hotter object cools down and the cooler object warms up until they match. Heat never flows on its own from a cooler object to a hotter one. This is why a hot drink cools to room temperature and a cold drink warms up.

items.prompt: A hot metal spoon is placed in cool water. Which way does heat flow, and what happens to their temperatures?

steps: Heat flows from the hotter object to the cooler one.
The spoon is hotter, so heat flows from the spoon to the water.
The spoon cools and the water warms until they reach the same temperature.
solution.answer: Heat flows from the hot spoon to the cool water; the spoon cools and the water warms until they are the same temperature.

steps: When two objects exchange heat, their temperatures change.
Thermal equilibrium is when they reach the same temperature and heat stops flowing between them.
At that point, no more net heat flows.
solution.answer: The state where two objects reach the same temperature and no more net heat flows between them.

items.prompt: Why does a hot drink cool down to room temperature?

steps: The drink is hotter than the surrounding room.
Heat flows from the hotter drink to the cooler surroundings.
This continues until the drink reaches room temperature, so it cools down.
solution.answer: Heat flows from the hotter drink to the cooler room until the drink reaches room temperature.

items.prompt: Does heat flow from the hotter object to the cooler one, or the other way?

steps: Heat flows in a specific direction on its own.
It flows from the hotter object to the cooler one.
solution.answer: From the hotter object to the cooler one.

items.prompt: A cold can of soda is left on a warm table. Predict the energy flow and the result.

steps: The table and air are warmer than the cold soda.
Heat flows from the warmer surroundings into the cooler soda.
The soda warms up until it reaches the same temperature as the surroundings.
solution.answer: Heat flows from the warm surroundings into the cold soda, warming it until it matches the surroundings' temperature.

items.prompt: Explain why heat never flows on its own from a cold object to a hot one.

steps: On its own, heat flows from hotter to cooler.
This continues until both are the same temperature.
It never spontaneously flows the other way, from cold to hot, because that is the opposite of the natural direction.
solution.answer: Because heat naturally flows only from hotter to cooler until they match, it never flows on its own from cold to hot.
